key_insight: Aligning model attention with pathologists’ viewing behavior improves prostate histopathology report generation and makes the model’s highlighted regions more clinically meaningful.
clinical_relevance: This could help produce more interpretable automated pathology reports and better support tasks like cancer characterization and visual question answering from whole-slide images.
method: Collected a multimodal attention dataset from 121 prostate WSIs with synchronized viewport trajectories, cursor movements, and verbal descriptions.
Finetuned two report-generation models using an attention-alignment loss to match model patch attention to pathologist attention.
Evaluated performance on prostate cancer report generation and visual question answering across five clinically relevant report components.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average gains of 10.9% on NLP-based metrics and 19.3% accuracy across five report components, with improved alignment between inference-time attention maps and pathologist attention.
watch_item: The approach was tested on a relatively small, single-disease dataset, so broader validation is needed before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Pathologist Attention-Aligned Report Generation for Prostate Histopathology
